title: Matrix Is All You Need: Rearchitecting Quantum Chemistry to Scale on AI Accelerators
problem: Quantum chemistry has irregular computation patterns, fragmented hardware utilization, and limited reach on modern AI accelerators (GPUs).
motivation: Scientific computing mismatch with AI accelerator execution model (low-precision matrix ops); quantum chemistry needs GPU scaling.
method: Mako transforms quantum chemistry calculations into matrix operations—the computations that GPUs are optimized to handle. It has three components: KernelMako converts the mathematical core (electron repulsion integrals, or ERI) into matrix multiplications using CUTLASS, an NVIDIA library for efficient matrix operations; QuantMako applies physics-aware compression to reduce data size while preserving accuracy; and CompilerMako combines operations together and customizes them for specific hardware. This restructuring allows GPUs to execute quantum chemistry workloads efficiently instead of leaving them underutilized.
key_novelty: The core idea is restructuring quantum chemistry's irregular computation patterns into regular matrix operations that AI accelerators like GPUs are optimized to handle efficiently.
contributions: ubiquitin (1231 atoms) from days to 58 minutes
limitations: Specific to quantum chemistry; applicability to other irregular scientific workloads unclear.
